# Chapter 1: Basic mathematics

<!-- BEGIN HEADER (generated by tools/build.py) -->
> [Home](../../../../README.md) › [Part I — Computer Science Foundations](../../index.md) › [2. Mathematics for Computer Science](../index.md) › Chapter 1: Basic mathematics

- **Status:** Drafted · 9 syllabus topics
<!-- END HEADER -->

This chapter is the foundation of the whole subject: the arithmetic, algebra and function notation that every later chapter takes for granted. It is taught with a programmer's eye, so each idea comes with the place where a computer's version differs from the version taught at school.

The first lesson covers numbers and their relationships: integer division and remainders, rounding, exact fractions, percentages and ratios. The second covers exponents and logarithms, which explain why binary search is fast, why 2⁶⁴ is enormous and how many bits a number needs. The third covers algebra, equations, inequalities and functions: how to turn a problem into an equation, and why a function in mathematics is not always a function in code. Short Python programs, and one short C program, make each idea concrete.

Later chapters build on this one: discrete mathematics, logic, graph theory, linear algebra, probability, statistics, calculus and numerical mathematics. Read the lessons in order.
